instruction: Change the text color of all numbers in the table on Page 3 to red.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing all table text to red color. Since the instruction mentions 'red' as a color name (not a specific hex code), the evaluator uses fuzzy color matching to check if the text color is visually red-like, with tolerance for theme variations.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical semantic mismatch: Instruction requires checking 'all numbers' but evaluator checks ALL text in the table
Evaluator does not distinguish between numeric and non-numeric text content
Will incorrectly fail if table headers/labels remain non-red even when all numbers are correctly colored red
Missing logic to identify and filter numeric text (e.g., using regex or type checking)
The evaluator would pass only if ALL text (including non-numeric) is red, which is NOT what the instruction requires
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add logic to identify numeric text: check if cell text can be parsed as a number (int/float) or matches numeric patterns
Filter cells/runs to only check those containing numeric values
Example fix: Add 'is_numeric()' helper to check if text represents a number, then only verify color for numeric text
Consider edge cases: currency symbols ($100), percentages (50%), decimal numbers (3.14), negative numbers (-5)
Alternative: Use regex pattern to identify numeric text: r'^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$' or similar
